A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAN+SR work and retain matching methods and core benchmarks. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Supplementary Section 4 report original benchmarking and variable-selection experiments on PMLB and extended Feynman datasets.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D retain original benchmarking results and add comparator evaluations, clustering ablations and predictor-robustness simulations.

M1.justification: Both versions average VIP rankings from 20 independent BART fits, apply Euclidean average-linkage hierarchical clustering, and retain the low-mean cluster before SR. These details already appear in v1 Supplementary Section 3.2; v2's expanded explanation and ablations do not establish a changed proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The 35 PMLB and 100 extended Feynman problems remain. Appendix D.4 adds Friedman-based variable-selection tests with predictor noise, a redundant feature x6 = x1 + x2, and correlated predictors. This is a bounded extension of the represented input conditions.

E2.justification: Figures 1–2 add DySymNet and TPSR to the 17 existing SR methods. Appendix D.2 adds PySR's random-forest selector to the three BART selector alternatives and introduces BART-G.SE+Operon in the downstream comparison with VIP Rank+Operon and standalone Operon. These substantially broaden the directly evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: The original splits, metrics, evaluation budgets and sample-size/SNR grid remain. New protocols include five-fold cross-validation over k = 1–20 for RF selection and controlled Friedman scenarios with n = 1000, p = 100 and SNR = 10, specified predictor-noise variance, and correlation structure.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's noise/sample-size sensitivity and ranking analyses, v2 adds downstream replacement of VIP Rank by BART-G.SE, a ten-algorithm clustering ablation, and noisy/redundant/correlated-predictor tests in Appendices D.2–D.4. These directly examine component choices and input assumptions that v1 did not test.

E5.justification: Appendix D.4 newly specifies 100 trials per Friedman scenario. Both versions retain ten seeded trials for the original benchmarks and 95% confidence intervals. V2 also explicitly identifies the confidence intervals in the retained Operon appendix plots; it does not report increasing repetitions of the original experiments.

E6.justification: V2 adds results for the new comparators, clustering ablations, predictor scenarios and the Operon solution-rate grid. New Table 3 reports R2 values of 0.892, 0.860 and 0.846 for VIP+SR, GSE+SR and standalone SR at n = 500 and SNR = 20. Table 4 reports 100% TPR across four scenarios, with FPR ranging from 10.58% to 26.42%.

T1.justification: After matching v1's q0 to v2's p0, Section 4 corrects the irrelevant-feature rank support from {p0, ..., p} to {p0 + 1, ..., p}, changing its expected mean from (p0 + p)/2 to (p0 + 1 + p)/2. This is a limited mathematical correction; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and discussion extend the claimed performance benefit from 17 to 19 SR methods, with the real-data claim changing from 16/17 to 18/19. The central contributions—nonparametric prescreening for scalable SR and high-dimensional benchmark construction—remain the same.

C2.justification: V2 explains the relevance of class imbalance to clustering choice and interprets the new robustness tests. The discussion newly acknowledges physical inconsistencies in the Feynman benchmark and describes complementary refinements from Matsubara et al. The existing cautions about low-SNR screening failures and noise-sensitive SR remain.

D1.justification: The stated repository changes from Scalable_SR to PAN_SR. Appendix B clarifies sampling and the sample variance used to set response noise, while Appendix D supplies RF tuning information and a scikit-learn version for the clustering ablation. Existing BART hyperparameters, hardware and reproduction commands are largely retained.

R1.justification: V2 expands positioning against PySR's RF prescreening and Matsubara et al.'s benchmark. It adds references including Chipman et al., DySymNet, Friedman and materials applications, while removing the Rockova–van der Pas and Luo–Li citations. The central positioning as an extension of SRBench to high-dimensional SR remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, method explanation, results narrative and discussion undergo substantial rewriting. Section 4 gains a detailed BART/VIP explanation and worked example. The separate supplement is reorganized into integrated Appendices A–D, with ranking visualization separated from selector comparisons and new analysis subsections.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text and extensively redraws and rearranges plots, including colors, legends and panel arrangements. It adds Tables 3–4 and clustering and solution-rate figures, expands comparator displays, and splits v1's supplementary Figure 5 into Figures 11–12.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central design choices: RF and downstream BART-G.SE comparisons test the selector's value, and the clustering ablation supports choosing hierarchical clustering. Predictor-robustness tests address assumptions untested in v1, while the expanded explanation and benchmark limitations improve assessability. The Friedman evidence remains limited to screening on one function, and Table 1 retains unchanged comparison totals despite added methods, but these reporting limitations are outweighed by the stronger empirical justification.
